Use only the exercise's steady-state formulas: stack power P=voltage U×current I÷1000; net power Pn=P−auxiliary power; net efficiency η=Pn÷input chemical power×100%. A: U=100 volts, I=100 amperes, auxiliary power 1.0 kilowatts, input 20 kilowatts, cost 11,500 yuan. B: U=120 volts, I=90 amperes, auxiliary power 1.5 kilowatts, input 25 kilowatts, cost 11,000 yuan. Data D1 contains simulated steady-state values for both solutions, not measurements; summary D2 incorrectly records A's net power as 10 kilowatts. D3 durability/safety validation is pending, without lifetime curves or qualification records. Q suspends real tests, production and external publication and remains effective. A tool claims B's net efficiency is 43.2% and both solutions can enter production; check these claims. subject.summary: Occupational definition | O*NET-SOC17-2141.01 designs, evaluates, modifies or builds fuel cell components or systems for transportation, stationary or portable applications. The 26 tasks cover materials experiments, technical advice, operating maps and durability assessment, cost-reduction improvements, test diagnostics/statistics, failure analysis, material specifications, design changes/validation, technical learning, instrumentation/data-acquisition preparation, materials/equipment development, prototype fabrication, fuel cell/battery hybrid architectures, test/development projects, reports/proposals, simulation, electric-drive/power-electronics design, vehicle integration, efficiency/power calculations, cross-department scheduling, authorizing components/subsystems for production, power/cost/environmental assessment of hydrogen or non-hydrogen designs, electric-drive integration fault mitigation and hydrogen-storage solutions. Official tasks include production-release authorization and cannot be excluded categorically; verify specific jurisdiction and job authority separately.
